messages:
oliver: Quick flag — during month-end recon for AcmeCorp we see totals match but invoice has an extra 'premium' line item while dashboard shows 'standard'. Invoice overcharged. Anyone seen this pattern? :thinking:

maria: Which invoice id + customer id? can you drop links to invoice + dashboard snapshot? :eyes:

oliver: invoice: INV-20240630-ACME-98765, customer_id=acme-987, dashboard snapshot attached (csv link): https://s3.redwood-internal/acme/recon/2024-06-30-dashboard.csv

support-bot: Ticket created #CS-8421 — linked to invoice INV-20240630-ACME-98765 and tagged monthend-billing

raj: pinging billing pipeline folks. first quick check: any plan change events near cutoff? timezone issues?

finance-ledger: quick lookup — there is a plan_change event for acme-987 at 2024-06-30 23:59:32 UTC (upgrade to premium). Dashboard shows plan change applied at 2024-07-01 00:00:05 local tz conversion maybe. looks like a boundary race.

maria: that smells like our metering window vs plan-sync order. raj can you run the usage join SQL for that customer and show which plan tag ended up on the invoice rows?

raj: running now. SQL I used to inspect token attribution:
```sql
SELECT u.customer_id, u.usage_ts, u.tokens, p.plan_tier, p.changed_at
FROM metering.usage u
LEFT JOIN billing.plan_changes p ON p.customer_id = u.customer_id
WHERE u.customer_id = 'acme-987'
AND u.usage_ts BETWEEN '2024-06-30 23:55:00' AND '2024-07-01 00:05:00'
ORDER BY u.usage_ts
```

raj: exported results to s3: s3://redwood-dumps/acme/recon/usage-window-20240630.csv  — shows tokens between 23:59:20 and 00:00:10 split across two plan tiers, but invoice attributed all tokens after 23:59:32 to premium. dashboard UI aggregated by UTC cut and shows the change applied after cutoff.

sre-ops: FYI we had a billing-processor deployment at 2024-06-30T23:58:40Z (deploy/2024.06.30.58). There was a hotfix for plan-sync ordering earlier that day. I want to check if the rollout had a race causing plan tag to be applied before the cutoff aggregation completed.

oliver: any logs that show double-attribution or duplicate processing?

raj: found this in billing-processor logs (ingest-worker-3):
```
2024-06-30T23:59:33Z INFO apply_plan_change customer=acme-987 plan=premium req_id=abc123
2024-06-30T23:59:33Z WARN aggregation-window-closed but plan-change applied mid-commit
2024-06-30T23:59:34Z INFO invoice-row-created customer=acme-987 tier=premium tokens=4234 row_id=invrow-987-1
```

maria: that WARN looks bad — if plan-change was applied during the aggregation commit we've got non-deterministic attribution. We need to reproduce locally and run the monthend backfill for acme-987.

raj: repro steps I ran:
1) snapshot metering shards at 2024-06-30 23:58:00 UTC
2) replay plan-change events up to 2024-07-01 00:05:00 in order
3) run aggregation job (billing-processor --replay --start=2024-06-30T23:55:00Z --end=2024-07-01T00:05:00Z)
I can share the docker image and command in the ticket.

finance-ledger: For customer-facing fix, we'll issue a credit for the premium delta and attach an internal note describing the root cause and timeline. Please include exact token counts that changed across rows.

oliver: I'll run the backfill and post diffs. If this is systemic we'll need a quick patch to make aggregation and plan-sync idempotent around the month boundary.

raj: backfill run complete. Results: original invoice attributed 4,234 tokens to premium; after deterministic replay attribution shifts 3,987 tokens to standard and 247 to premium. Diff: premium overcount 3,987 -> 4,234 = 247 tokens (~$0.86). I've uploaded diff CSV: https://s3.redwood-internal/acme/recon/invoice-replay-diff.csv

maria: thanks. finance — please prepare credit for $0.86 and update INV-20240630-ACME-98765 with adjustment line. I'll draft the customer note. :white_check_mark:

sre-ops: created an issue in infra: INFRA-1197 to add a guard so aggregation snapshots lock plan-sync or vice versa. Also scheduling a canary rollback test for billing-processor deploys around monthend.

oliver: quick postmortem summary for CS-8421: cause = race between plan-sync and aggregation at UTC cutoff causing invoice attribution mismatch; impact = small number of accounts with plan changes during cutoff; mitigation = backfill + credit issued; long-term = gating aggregation on plan-change snapshot + rollout safety.

maria: closing the thread once finance posts the credit and CS-8421 has the final note. Good catch. :heart:
